issues.claim: Legal section: "New Jersey has not enacted an employer-facing biometric privacy statute" is marked confirmed:true and sourced to the A3929 bill text.
issues.problem: The cited page is the text of a pending consumer-facing bill; it says nothing about whether an employer-facing biometric statute exists or not. The negative is probably true but is unsupported by the cited source, yet it is presented as confirmed.
issues.fix: Re-source the absence claim to a page that actually states it (e.g. the recordinglaw.com New Jersey biometric-privacy page), or reword to "no employer-facing New Jersey biometric statute was identified in this session" and mark it as research finding rather than confirmed rule.

issues.claim: Legal section, "Documented hygiene monitoring duty and bare-hand contact": the N.J.A.C. 8:24-8.13 inspection-report-on-premises rule (most recent report kept for public review, at least two years) is cited to the 8:24-3.3 URL.
issues.problem: The rule is real - I confirmed it verbatim - but it is not on the cited page. 8:24-3.3 contains only the hand/bare-hand-contact provisions, so the citation does not support the sentence it is attached to.
issues.fix: Add a separate citation to https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/new-jersey/N-J-A-C-8-24-8-13 for the 8.13 sentence (keep 8:24-3.3 for the (a)2/(a)4 sentence).

issues.claim: Pilot cost_range: "Roughly $4,000-9,000 one-time per site", built from "hardware about $1,300-2,000" plus "40-70 hours ... at $75-125/hour = $3,000-8,750".
issues.problem: The stated range does not follow from its own components: $1,300-2,000 + $3,000-8,750 = $4,300-10,750. Both the bottom ($4,000) and top ($9,000) of the published range are inconsistent with the arithmetic. The $150-400/month ongoing figure is also not derived from anything in the section.
issues.fix: Restate as $4,300-10,750 one-time (or round to $4,500-11,000), and show one line of arithmetic for the monthly figure (e.g. support hours + hosting) or mark it explicitly as an unanchored estimate.

issues.claim: Miso Flippy: "Vision-guided robot that dispenses, fries and baskets fries at roughly 100 baskets/hour".
issues.problem: The press release says the new Flippy "can process more than 100 baskets per hour - almost twice as many as humans". "Roughly 100" understates and drops the "more than" qualifier.
issues.fix: Change to "more than 100 baskets per hour (vendor claim, nearly twice human throughput)".

issues.claim: KITRO is described as "the device used in the 2025 peer-reviewed HORECA trial".
issues.problem: ReFED's summary (the source actually read) describes five foodservice sites in Germany, Greece and Switzerland and does not use the term HORECA; the "HORECA" label is imported and unverified.
issues.fix: Say "the device used in the five-site 2025 European foodservice study summarised by ReFED (May 2026)".

claims_checked.claim: Foodservice generated 12.5M tons of surplus in 2024, valued at $156B = 11% of foodservice sales; 78.4% of food waste (9.73M tons) went to landfill.
More than 43% of restaurant/foodservice surplus came from full-service restaurants and nearly 70% from plate waste.
Median food and non-alcoholic beverage cost 32.0% of sales (full service) and 32.4% (limited service) in 2024.
Median labor cost including benefits 36.5% of sales (full service) and 31.7% (limited service) in 2024.

FDA 1998-2008 study: proper and adequate handwashing in compliance in 24% of observations at full-service and 61% at fast-food restaurants; poor personal hygiene 59%/76% in 2008; improper holding 45% full service; ~850 establishments per phase.
N.J.A.C. 8:24-2.1(c)3.i obliges the person in charge to ensure handwashing through "routinely monitoring the employees' handwashing"; amended effective 12/20/2021.

N.J.A.C. 8:24-3.3(a)2 bars bare-hand contact with exposed ready-to-eat food; (a)4 allows it for establishments not serving a highly susceptible population if they keep written procedures, food lists, handwashing-facility diagrams and training-acknowledgement documentation.
N.J.A.C. 8:24-8.13 requires the most recent inspection report on premises for public review for at least two years.

Two million US restaurant inspections (Sept 2022-Sept 2023): handwashing the top FDA-food-code violation area, nearly 6% of inspections for inadequate handwashing stations; 15% among a 17-brand hospitality subset.
Hourly turnover 96% (full service) and 135% (limited service) as of Q3 2024.
Middlesex County: 1,752 Accommodation and Food Services establishments employing 24,124 people, QCEW 2024.

HME Nitro Vision AI (April 2025) gives "real-time awareness of customers' total wait times, including mobile order pick-up zones"; built on acquired Agot AI vision; drive-thru focus; no price published.
Winnow VisionAI listed on AWS Marketplace at an approximate baseline near $10,000 per site (typical annual contract value), varying with kitchen size/complexity.
Miso Flippy Fry Station: $5,400/month rental, no upfront cost; "more than 100 baskets per hour".
Kitchen display systems roughly $20-30 per screen per month across major KDS vendors in 2026 comparisons; Toast sells by quote.
Ubiquiti G5 Flex: $129.00 list, $151.00 with surcharges, 2K HD PoE.
Ubiquiti Lite 8 PoE (USW-Lite-8-POE): $109.00 list, $120.00 with surcharge, 8 ports, 52W total PoE availability.
Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit: $249 (down from $499), 67 INT8 TOPS, 8GB, supports up to four cameras.
Ohaus Valor 2000 30 kg x 5 g, NSF-certified, IPX8: $479.95 at a US retailer (retail list $710.00); no USB/PC interface stated.
Ultralytics YOLO is AGPL-3.0 by default and an Enterprise licence is required for commercial/proprietary/embedded deployment.
RT-DETR is Apache-2.0 and a real-time detector.
LFM2-VL model card recommends fine-tuning on narrow use cases and states the models are "not intended for safety-critical decisions".

Journal of Imaging 6(11):120 (published 7 November 2020): 86.36% for "apply soap", 93.18% for "dry hands", 95.45% for "touch faucet with elbow"; duration error 2.39 s and 2.20 s; heavy classifiers on 67.8% of frames; 100 participants, two public restrooms, three camera views.

2026 Nature food-handler study: 46 handlers at NUS student canteens, two visits, 44 completed both, 43 survey responses; authors state the study cannot fully separate AI guidance from procedural standardisation, timed washing, camera observation or increased awareness.

2025 five-site KITRO study: waste per meal down 23-51% at four of five sites, prep waste down >80%, overproduction cost down 48-69%, avoidable waste cost per meal down up to 39%; no-improvement site was a Swiss hotel with low management engagement and high turnover.
Winnow vendor claim: average 42% food-waste reduction in the first six months, over 50% over longer periods.

About 16% of quick-service and fast-casual orders have problems customers notice and report; one chain's annual cost of inaccuracy exceeded $26 million; page carries no date and promotes "the 2022 QSR results".
Third-party directory states Agot AI's kitchen vision "spots 85%+ of order errors in real time".
New Jersey has no statute requiring employer notice/signage for ordinary workplace video cameras; N.J.S.A. 34:6B-22 covers only tracking devices in vehicles used by employees.
Under N.J.S.A. 2C:14-9(d) prior posted/provided notice is an affirmative defence only if the actor also acted with a lawful purpose (both elements required).
New Jersey is one-party consent for private in-person conversations under the Wiretapping Act (N.J.S.A. 2A:156A-2/-3/-4).
N.J.S.A. 2C:14-9 criminalises observing or recording a person without consent where a reasonable person would not expect to be observed (intimate parts, sexual acts, undressing).

A3929 (2026 session) would regulate biometric surveillance of consumers on business premises with conspicuous notice; as of the legislature's listed actions it had passed the Assembly and been referred to a Senate committee, so it is not law.

NLRB GC memo GC 23-02 (October 31, 2022) announced a framework treating intrusive electronic monitoring that tends to interfere with Section 7 rights as presumptively unlawful and urged disclosure of technologies used and why.

FTC advertising-substantiation policy: advertisers must have a reasonable basis for express and implied objective claims before dissemination; absence of a reasonable basis is an unfair/deceptive practice under Section 5; "tests prove"/"studies show" claims require at least that level of support.
